$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(2{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(2{y}^{2}+{y}^{-2}) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-2}) \\  & =4y-2{y}^{-3} \\  & =4y-\frac{2}{{y}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{4{y}^{4}-2}{{y}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\dfrac{\textrm dx}{\textrm dy},$ we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm dy}{\textrm dx} = \left( \dfrac{\textrm dx}{\textrm dy} \right)^{-1} = \dfrac{y^3}{4y^4 -2}.
$$"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "00ac6edc-908a-50be-9ef1-4b24ba597d1d" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186048932 :topic/id #uuid "cd2e9db4-6727-5887-90bc-20eb0a0bf6d2" :topic/knowledge-points [{:db/id 17592186059862} {:db/id 17592186059863} {:db/id 17592186059864} {:db/id 17592186059865}] :topic/math-academy-id 278 :topic/next [{:db/id 17592186048442} {:db/id 17592186050711}] :topic/title "The Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Differentiation"} {:db/id 17592186050310 :topic/encompasses [{:db/id 17592186429224 :encompassing/rationale "Initial Codex estimate from captured target-band crossing frequency. proposals.after:
Given that $x=-\frac{2}{{y}^{2}}+5{y}^{2},$ express $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ as a function of $y.$
$\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=$ ${y}^{3}$ {{field-1}}

proposals.before:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-\frac{2}{{y}^{2}}+5{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-2{y}^{-1}+5{y}^{2}) \\  & =-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-2})+5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =-2(-2{y}^{-3})+5(2y) \\  & =\frac{4}{{y}^{3}}+10y \\  & =\frac{4+10{y}^{4}}{{y}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y}\right)}^{-1}=\frac{{y}^{3}}{4+10{y}^{4}}.
$$
proposals.after:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-\frac{2}{{y}^{2}}+5{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-2{y}^{-2}+5{y}^{2}) \\  & =-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-2})+5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =-2(-2{y}^{-3})+5(2y) \\  & =\frac{4}{{y}^{3}}+10y \\  & =\frac{4+10{y}^{4}}{{y}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y}\right)}^{-1}=\frac{{y}^{3}}{4+10{y}^{4}}.
$$
